answer: Bind each identity to a scarce physical-rooted credential that can only be minted after a peer-attested compute task on real silicon. Creating a thousand clones forces the attacker to acquire a thousand distinct chips and burn the corresponding bonds; the cost scales linearly with head-count and cannot be virtualized. On the tundra of cheap software identities the pigment of hardware attestation stands out, and only agents that survive the mesa of repeated live challenges keep their stake.
